statement: A tree is determined up to isomorphism by the spectrum of its adjacency matrix.
definitions: Trees are finite, simple, unlabelled. The spectrum of a tree is the multiset of eigenvalues of its 0/1 adjacency matrix, equivalently its characteristic polynomial. A counterexample is a pair of non-isomorphic trees with the same characteristic polynomial (for trees this equals the matching polynomial sum_k (-1)^k m_k x^{n-2k}), together with a verification of cospectrality and of non-isomorphism (e.g. differing degree sequences).
ground_truth_witness: T1 on V={0,...,7}, E=[[0,1],[0,6],[1,2],[1,3],[1,4],[1,5],[6,7]] (a spider: vertex 1 has four leaves 2,3,4,5 plus a path 1-0-6-7); T2 on V={0,...,7}, E=[[0,1],[0,5],[0,6],[0,7],[1,2],[1,3],[1,4]] (a double star: adjacent centres 0 and 1, each with three leaves). Both are trees with characteristic polynomial x^8 - 7x^6 + 9x^4, but their degree sequences are (5,2,2,1,1,1,1,1) and (4,4,1,1,1,1,1,1), so they are not isomorphic. This is the unique cospectral pair among the 23 trees on 8 vertices, and no cospectral pair of trees exists on fewer vertices.
reference_authority: online-cited counterexample (MO/MSE/CS.SE/Wikipedia) with verify script, verified per partB_feasibility records

skeptic.objection: Claim (a tree is determined by its adjacency spectrum) is false; reference verified exactly: for trees the characteristic polynomial is the matching polynomial, and both T1 (spider: vertex with four leaves plus a path of length 3) and T2 (double star S(3,3)) have matching numbers m1 = 7, m2 = 9, m3 = 0, i.e. x^8 - 7x^6 + 9x^4, while their degree sequences (5,2,2,1,1,1,1,1) vs (4,4,1,1,1,1,1,1) differ. I enumerated all non-isomorphic trees on 2..8 vertices (1,1,2,3,6,11,23 of them): no cospectral pair exists on <= 7 vertices and this is the unique cospectral pair on 8, exactly as the reference states. Not a duplicate: the roster/surplus cospectral items use K_{1,4} vs C4 + K1 (not trees) or strongly regular graphs, and the restriction to trees defeats those witnesses. Refutation requires constructing two trees and computing/comparing their characteristic polynomials -- genuine work, since the famous fact 'almost all trees are cospectral' (Schwenk) gives no explicit pair.
